transcript.text: Good morning, Dr. Morgan. As the Instructional Technology Coordinator, I've completed my technology review of the proposed oral-history project, and I have several critical findings to share. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, all source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. I want to note that storing source files in the restricted OralHistory drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website, so that element can still move forward with proper consent. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record before the project can be approved.
